transfers.source_mechanism: adaptive network formation through feedback-driven structural optimization
transfers.target_problem: A mid-sized city (population 800,000) has a traffic signal network with 247 signalized intersections. The current signal timing plan is optimized centrally every 6 months using a macroscopic traffic model, but it cannot adapt to real-time conditions: incidents, weather, special events, and construction. Re-optimizing centrally every minute is computationally infeasible and would require expensive predictive models. The city wants a distributed, adaptive signal timing approach that uses only local traffic flow measurements (vehicle count and queue length at each intersection) to adjust green-split and offset in real time, without a central optimizer.
transfers.transferred_principle: distributed feedback-driven optimization of traffic signal timing using local measurements and neighbor communication
transfers.required_translation: replace nutrient resources with traffic flow, sensory input with loop detector measurements, network structure with traffic signal connections, and network reconfiguration with signal timing adjustments. Physical substitution: replace protoplasmic streaming with vehicle flow, pseudopods with green time allocation, and chemical signals with timing offset messages between adjacent signals.
transfers.expected_effect: self-organized traffic signal network that adapts timing in real-time to changing conditions without central optimization
boundary_conditions: limited local measurements (vehicle count + queue length)
transfers.testable_prediction: Under incident conditions, the distributed system will converge to a new stable timing plan within 15 minutes that reduces overall delay by at least 15% compared to the fixed-timing baseline, as measured by average travel time through the network
